exercises.audioText: Researchers have long wondered how some animals sleep while remaining alert to danger. Certain birds, for instance, can rest one half of their brain at a time, keeping one eye open. This ability, called unihemispheric sleep, helps them watch for predators even while resting. Scientists are now studying whether similar mechanisms might explain sleep patterns in other species.

options: They sleep with both halves of the brain.
They rest one half of the brain at a time.
exercises.explanation: B — "can rest one half of their brain at a time, keeping one eye open."

exercises.audioText: When the printing press spread across Europe in the 15th century, it revolutionized not only the cost of books, but also the very nature of information dissemination. Prior to this invention, ideas and knowledge often took years, if not decades, to traverse the vast distances between regions, limiting the exchange of thoughts and cultural practices. However, with the advent of the printing press, this dynamic shifted dramatically. Information that once traveled at a snail's pace could now be reproduced and circulated in a matter of months, allowing for a rapid exchange of ideas across borders. This monumental change laid the essential groundwork for widespread literacy as more individuals gained access to printed materials. Furthermore, it catalyzed public discourse and debate, enabling discussions on social, political and philosophical issues to flourish on an unprecedented scale. The printing press not only democratized knowledge, but also fostered a more informed and engaged populace, paving the way for the Enlightenment and modern democratic societies.
exercises.question: When did the printing press spread across Europe?
exercises.explanation: B — "When the printing press spread across Europe in the 15th century…"

exercises.audioText: Urban gardens provide far more than fresh produce. They play a pivotal role in mitigating urban heat, particularly during severe heat waves. These green spaces are invaluable because plants not only absorb sunlight, but also release moisture through transpiration, a natural process that helps reduce ambient temperatures and create a more comfortable environment for residents. Cities that have invested in the development and upkeep of urban gardens have reported significant declines in local temperatures during the hottest summer months. In addition, these gardens improve air quality by filtering pollutants and producing oxygen, thereby contributing to healthier urban living conditions. Their presence also nurtures a stronger sense of community and encourages outdoor activity, further enhancing the well-being of city dwellers. Overall, urban gardens are essential to building sustainable, livable cities, offering ecological, social, and health benefits that extend well beyond their aesthetic value.
exercises.question: How do plants help cool cities?
options: By absorbing sunlight and releasing moisture through transpiration.
exercises.explanation: B — "plants not only absorb sunlight, but also release moisture through transpiration."

Woman: Perfect, thank you.
N: Now answer the questions.

Woman: Welcome. Can I see your ID, please? I'll print your visitor badge.
Man: Here you go. Am I early? It's only nine forty.
Woman: That's fine — most candidates arrive fifteen minutes early. The interview is on the fourth floor, room four-oh-two.
Man: Should I bring anything besides my resume?
Woman: Just yourself. She already has your application. The elevator is around the corner, and I'll call up to let her know you're here.
Man: Thanks very much.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: How early did he arrive for a ten o'clock interview?
exercises.explanation: A — "It's only nine forty" for a ten o'clock interview.

Man: Then you're all set. I'll email your final receipt within an hour. Was the mileage under the limit?
Woman: Yes, I drove about three hundred miles.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: What problem does the woman report?
options: A new scratch on the car.
exercises.explanation: B — "the GPS stopped working on the second day."

N: Now answer the questions.

options: Two at night on an empty stomach.

N: Listen to a conversation with IT support.
Woman: Hi, my laptop won't connect to the office Wi-Fi since this morning.
Man: Are other devices connecting? Let's check if it's your laptop or the network.
Woman: My phone connects fine, so it's the laptop.
Man: Okay, first restart it, then forget the network called Office-Secure and join it again with your usual password.
Woman: I tried restarting twice already.
Man: Then I'll reset your network profile from here. Give me one minute. After that, try again and tell me what error you see.
Woman: Now it asks for a certificate. What do I press?
Man: Choose accept, then enter your login once more.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: What is the woman's problem?
options: Her laptop will not connect to the office Wi-Fi.
exercises.explanation: A — "my laptop won't connect to the office Wi-Fi since this morning."

N: Listen to a conversation at a farmers market.
Man: Good morning! Are these tomatoes local?
Woman: Yes, picked yesterday about twenty miles from here. Two dollars a pound, or three pounds for five.
Man: I'll take three pounds. Do you have fresh basil too?
Woman: The last bunch sold ten minutes ago, but more arrives at eleven.
Man: I can't wait that long. Do you take cards?
Woman: Yes, cards and cash. Bags cost ten cents, or you can use your own bag for free.
Man: I brought mine. Are you here every Saturday?
Woman: Every Saturday until October, same spot near the entrance.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: What is the tomato deal?
options: Two dollars a pound, or three pounds for five.
exercises.explanation: A — "Two dollars a pound, or three pounds for five."

N: Listen to a short job interview in a café.
Woman: So why do you want to work here part-time?
Man: I'm a student nearby, and I need morning shifts before classes. I also like talking to customers.

Woman: Good. We train for one week, paid. Can you start Monday at seven?
Man: Yes. Should I bring anything?
Woman: Just your ID and comfortable shoes.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: Which shifts does the man need?
exercises.explanation: B — "I need morning shifts before classes."

Man: Only if the doctor orders it. She'll tell you during the visit.
Woman: Okay, thank you.
N: Now answer the questions.

N: Listen to a conversation between neighbors.
Man: Hi, sorry to bother you. Are you doing construction? There's loud drilling every morning.
Woman: Oh, I'm so sorry — we're installing shelves. I didn't realize it carried through the walls.
Man: Could you start after nine? I work nights and sleep until eight-thirty.
Woman: Of course. We'll only drill between ten and noon from now on.
Man: Thanks. How long will the work last?
Woman: Just two more days. I'll leave a note for the other neighbors too.
Man: I appreciate that. Let me know if you need help moving anything heavy.
Woman: That's kind — I'll ask if we get stuck.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: What is making the noise?
exercises.explanation: B — "We're installing shelves" (morning drilling).

Woman: Hi, I'd like to join the Thursday cooking class.
Man: Great — beginners or advanced? Beginners cook Italian basics; advanced does sushi this month.

Woman: Can I still join if I miss one week?
Man: Yes, we'll send the recipe and you can catch up the next week.
N: Now answer the questions.

exercises.audioText:
N: Listen to a conversation at a community center.
Woman: Hi, I'd like to join the Thursday cooking class.
Man: Great — beginners or advanced? Beginners cook Italian basics; advanced does sushi this month.
Woman: Beginners, please. How much is it?
Man: Forty dollars for four weeks, including ingredients. Bring your own apron and a container for leftovers.
Woman: What time does it start?
Man: Six to eight in room three. The first class is knife skills, so please arrive ten minutes early.
Woman: Can I still join if I miss one week?
Man: Yes, we'll send the recipe and you can catch up the next week.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: What do beginners cook this month?
exercises.explanation: B — "Beginners cook Italian basics; advanced does sushi this month."

N: Listen to a radio travel update.
Man: If you're driving north tonight, expect heavy rain after eight and possible flooding near the river bridge. Police advise using the south highway instead — it adds fifteen minutes but stays on higher ground. Buses are running on schedule, though the nine-fifteen express is full. Trains to the coast are delayed by thirty minutes due to strong winds. Check the travel app before leaving, and keep headlights on even in light rain. We'll update again at the top of the hour.
N: Now answer the questions.

options: Heavy rain with possible flooding near the river bridge.
exercises.explanation: B — "expect heavy rain after eight and possible flooding near the river bridge."

exercises.audioText:
N: Listen to a conversation before a meeting.
Woman: Did you print the handouts for the ten o'clock meeting?
Man: I printed twenty copies, but the printer jammed on the last five. They're a bit smudged.
Woman: That's okay — twelve people confirmed, so twenty is plenty. Did you include the updated chart?
Man: Yes, page three has the new numbers from yesterday. I also saved the file on a USB stick in case we need to project it.
Woman: Perfect. Can you arrive five minutes early to set out chairs?
Man: Sure. I'll put handouts on each chair and test the projector.
Woman: Thanks — that saves us a rushed start.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: How many copies and attendees?
options: Twenty copies for twelve confirmed people.
exercises.explanation: A — "I printed twenty copies" + "Twelve people confirmed."

exercises.audioText:
N: Listen to two friends planning a weekend walk.
Man: Want to try the riverside trail on Sunday? It's about six miles and mostly flat.
Woman: Sounds good. What time? I have a podcast club at four.
Man: Let's start at nine, so we finish by noon with a lunch stop. Bring water — there's only one fountain at mile three.
Woman: Is the path okay after last week's rain?
Man: The city site says the hill section is muddy, but the river section is clear. We'll stick to the lower path.
Woman: Should I bring anything else?
Man: Just a rain jacket in case, and I'll bring the trail map.
N: Now answer the questions.
exercises.question: What is the trail like?
exercises.explanation: A — "It's about six miles and mostly flat."

exercises.audioText: One experience that taught me how to adapt was when my university suddenly moved an important course online. At first, I was disappointed because I enjoyed discussing ideas with my classmates in person, and I worried that I would not be able to concentrate at home. However, I decided to create a regular routine. I chose a quiet place to study, attended every virtual class, and wrote down questions before each meeting. I also contacted two classmates so that we could review difficult topics together. After a few weeks, I became more comfortable with the new system. In fact, I discovered that online learning gave me more time to review lessons and organize my notes. This experience showed me that unexpected changes can be difficult, but a clear routine and support from other people can make them much easier to manage.
exercises.question: Why was the speaker disappointed when the course moved online?
options: He enjoyed in-person discussion and feared he could not concentrate at home.
His classmates refused to help him.
exercises.explanation: B — "I enjoyed discussing ideas with my classmates in person, and I worried that I would not be able to concentrate at home."

exercises.audioText: In my opinion, cities should provide more public parks, even if they have to reduce spending on some less urgent projects. Parks are not simply attractive places; they also improve people's physical and mental health. Residents can walk, exercise, or relax outdoors without paying for a private facility. In addition, parks create spaces where neighbors from different backgrounds can meet and develop a stronger sense of community. They can also make crowded neighborhoods more pleasant and reduce the effects of heat during the summer. Of course, cities must consider their budgets carefully, and essential services should remain the priority. Nevertheless, investing in well-planned parks can save money in the long term by encouraging healthier lifestyles and improving the quality of urban life. For these reasons, I believe public parks are an important part of responsible city planning.
exercises.question: What is the speaker's opinion?
options: Cities should provide more parks even if less urgent projects get less money.
Parks are a waste of public money.
Only private parks are worth building.
exercises.explanation: A — "cities should provide more public parks, even if they have to reduce spending on some less urgent projects."

exercises.audioText: Working from home has several important advantages. First, employees do not need to spend time or money commuting, so they may have more energy for their jobs and personal lives. They can also create a comfortable work environment and sometimes organize their schedules more flexibly. For companies, remote work may reduce the cost of office space. However, there are disadvantages as well. Some people find it difficult to separate work from family responsibilities, and others may feel isolated because they have fewer face-to-face conversations with colleagues. Communication can also become slower when every question has to be answered through messages or video meetings. In my view, working from home is most effective when employees have a quiet workspace, clear expectations, and regular opportunities to interact with their teams. A mixed arrangement, with some days at home and some in the office, may offer the best balance for many workers.
exercises.question: Which advantage of working from home is mentioned?
exercises.explanation: A — "employees do not need to spend time or money commuting."
